workload.description: one-file cgo build timed inside an already-started native container

uncached_control_1m_ceiling.failure: guest did not exit after 1000000 traps

authority.one_million_traps_interpretation: invalid completion threshold: the successful profile required 19057383 aggregate gateway entries and its hottest thread exceeded the ceiling at 1520928 entries
authority.pathology: translation consumed 58308975785 ns, 53.38% of 109234585000 ns descendant CPU

two_consecutive_go_env.interpretation: simple Go startup and cross-exec reuse are correct

cgo_build_p1.interpretation: forcing Go package parallelism to one does not remove the deterministic replay corruption

reduction.next_diagnostic: compare replayed code and recovery metadata with a fresh emission at build-only artifact hits, then fall back before execution on the first mismatch

reason: The spike proves real cross-process reuse and low replay CPU, but both cache-enabled signed runs deterministically corrupt Go stack state. The uncached control completes correctly in 58.737 seconds versus Docker's 1.447 seconds (40.583x), and a successful process-tree profile attributes 58.309 CPU-seconds to translation. One million traps was only an invalid early cutoff. The cache remains the highest-leverage step-function hypothesis, but no successful paired speedup can be claimed until replay correctness is fixed; do not proceed to a production cache implementation.
